lines.trans: Thank goodness you are here, {M1}—we were afraid of bending the painted lid.
Never force old tin, {F1}; one tiny drop of warm oil loosens any rim.
How long does the oil need before we try turning the corners?
Count to five, press the centre gently with one thumb, and lift evenly.
One, two, three, four, five... it popped right open without a scratch!
Smell that? Cedar shavings, dry paper, and faint peppermint from thirty years ago.
Oh, {M1}, look at what is sitting right on top in a velvet pouch!
A solid brass pocket compass with a glass cover and a blued steel needle.
Watch the little needle spin as I set it flat on the wooden table!
Still balanced to the degree—pointing straight out the window past the shade tree.
Look inside the brass cover: there are tiny initials engraved beside a star.
A mapmaker never travels without a good compass, so leaving this behind meant a lot.
